reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared features across instances with external XAI tools to quantitatively assess feature attribution and spurious influence. This ensures both domain-level insight and model-level validation of feature importance.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features appear in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 35024) and list their values.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features with their values across all three instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether the shared features have a spurious correlation with the target label (e.g., due to indirect or coincidental patterns in the dataset).
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: An interpretation of whether the shared feature(s) are semantically unrelated to the actual class label

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP and LIME provide model-level attribution to identify features with high impact on predictions. Integrated gradients offer smooth gradient-based attribution across instances, while sensitivity analysis quantifies how prediction changes when features are removed, validating spuriousness. Together, these tools confirm whether shared features are high-attribution spurious signals not tied to the true class distribution.

parameters.reasoning: SHAP values provide a globally consistent measure of feature importance and allow for identifying which features have high attribution across misclassified cases, even if semantically unrelated. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability to validate whether the high attribution is consistent with the model's prediction logic. Sensitivity analysis helps isolate the causal impact of features by ablation, confirming whether removing a shared feature improves prediction accuracy, thus verifying spuriousness. Together, these tools cross-validate the autonomous findings with model-level evidence.
